parts.note: Napoleon here is not the French emperor but the pig who seizes power in George Orwell's novel; the clue asks for the farm he lives on, which is also the novel's title

explanation.surface: A question about where the French emperor lived, framed as something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Napoleon' suggests Bonaparte and 'novel' looks like 'new', but Napoleon is Orwell's tyrant pig, and the home is the farm that gives the novel its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's allegorical novel is set on the farm where the pig Napoleon rules, so the place and the book share the name.

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters of the word before it wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A frog-like creature that has wandered off.
explanation.definitionFit: A small salamander that lives partly in water is a classic example of an amphibian.

clue.text: African state; one under matriarchal rule

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece under another is written after it

parts.note: a matriarch is a mother figure, and MA is a familiar word for mother
a rule or statute is a law
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A country in Africa described as living under the rule of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matriarchal rule' reads as MA's LAW, mother's law; 'under' places the I for 'one' below it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked country in south-east Africa, so it is an African state.

indicators.note: making here means forming or producing, so the letters of the two words before it are made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone works on doggedly, producing creams.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotions are liquid preparations rubbed on the skin, much the same as ointments.

definitions.meaning: weapons collectively are ..., as in an ... race
the limbs from shoulder to hand are what sit inside the sleeves of a shirt

explanation.walkthrough: 'kept up one's sleeve' suggests a hidden trick or a concealed weapon, but literally it is the limbs inside your sleeves.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms means both weapons and the upper limbs that fill one's sleeves, giving two senses of one word.

parts.note: a chap is a man
an appointment or engagement to meet is a date

explanation.surface: An order for a fellow to take up a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official order or authority to act, so it is a command.

definitions.meaning: removing cash from a bank account is making a ...
retiring from a place or position is drawing back from it

explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawal is both removing funds from an account and the act of retiring or pulling back.

clue.text: Safe blower who started series of small explosions

definitions.text: who started series of small explosions

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a piper blows into his pipes

explanation.surface: A safecracker who set off a string of little blasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'small explosions' are the letter P sounds, plosives, in the tongue-twister 'Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers'; 'Safe blower' suggests a cracksman using explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery tongue-twister begins with this name and continues with a run of popping P sounds, which the clue calls small explosions.

indicators.note: something held by another sits inside its grip, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army soldiers

explanation.surface: A rebel is captured by troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise or rise up is to rebel against authority, as in a popular rising.

clue.text: He hasn't made the First XI

definitions.text: He hasn't made the First XI

parts.words: He hasn't made the First XI
parts.note: in cricket, the reserve player who fields as substitute is not one of the eleven selected, though he is numbered next after them

explanation.surface: A player who failed to get into the top cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket team has eleven players (the XI); the reserve who fields for an injured player is named after the eleventh, so he literally hasn't made the eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: The reserve in a cricket side is the one after the eleven selected players, so he is outside the First XI.

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the girl's name to the wordplay

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of the two words before it are put back together differently

explanation.surface: Someone's writing pen has snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne is a girl's name, from the nymph of Greek myth who became a laurel tree.

definitions.meaning: a flag flown on a ship to show its nationality is an ensign
in the US Navy, and formerly the British army, an ensign is a junior commissioned officer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag officers' is a naval term for admirals, but here the words split: flags, and junior officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensign names both a ship's national flag and a junior commissioned officer, so the plural serves both words.

parts.note: will here is a legal testament, and the hope it breeds is that of an heir waiting to inherit

explanation.surface: Optimism created by determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the will' looks like willpower, but it is a testament; heirs named in one live in hope of what is to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Expectancy is a state of hopeful anticipation, as felt by someone who stands to inherit.

definitions.meaning: goods that are not new have already been owned by someone else
a digital watch shows numbers, so it has none of the pointers that sweep round a dial counting off seconds

explanation.walkthrough: The split is after 'Used'; the second half describes the thin pointer on an analogue dial that digital watches lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand means previously owned, and is also the name of the pointer marking seconds on a clock face.

definitions.meaning: someone who remains in place ... there
supports, such as the ropes bracing a mast or the stiffening of a corset

explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains of' looks like leftovers of something; split it into a verb, 'remains', and a noun, 'support', with 'of' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays is both a verb meaning remains and a plural noun for supports such as rigging ropes or corsets.

definitions.meaning: a ... iron is the metal loop a rider puts a foot in
a farewell drink given to a rider about to set off

explanation.definitionFit: The metal footrest of a saddle is often called an iron, and a parting drink is the cup named after it.

clue.text: Instrument may be easier to play upside-down

definitions.text: Instrument may be easier to play upside-down

parts.words: Instrument may be easier to play upside-down
parts.note: the instrument is a famous violin; written the other way up its name spells a pub game thrown at a board, which is far easier to play

explanation.surface: A violin might be easier to play if held the wrong way up.
explanation.walkthrough: A Strad is a violin made by Stradivari; read upside-down (backwards in a down entry) it gives DARTS, a game simpler than the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Strad is the short name for a Stradivarius violin, one of the most prized of all instruments.

definitions.meaning: to say something formally is to declare or express it
a nation, its whole body of citizens taken together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Speak for' suggests representing someone; 'for' is only the link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: State is a verb meaning to say clearly and a noun for a nation or its people as a political whole.

definitions.meaning: to select one item
a ..., or pickaxe, is the tool used to break up hard earth

explanation.walkthrough: 'break new ground' normally means to innovate; read literally, it is the work of a pickaxe.
explanation.definitionFit: Pick is both a verb for selecting and a noun for a pointed digging tool used to break up ground.

clue.text: Exchange prisoners of war in return

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: POWs is the standard abbreviation for prisoners of war

explanation.surface: Captured soldiers are traded back to their own side.
explanation.definitionFit: A swop, more often spelt swap, is an exchange of one thing for another.

clue.text: How government works as a rule

definitions.meaning: a government acts according to law
a local regulation made by a council or company

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, BY LAW says how government acts; as one, it is a local regulation. 'as' links them.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-law is a regulation made by a local authority, which is a kind of rule.

clue.text: Flower blooms freely around the start of spring

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, so the reworked letters surround the single letter
freely means without fixed arrangement, so the letters of the word before it move into a new order
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A flower opens its petals widely as spring begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges BLOOMS into BLOSOM, and 'around' puts that round S, the first letter of 'spring'.
explanation.definitionFit: A blossom is a flower, especially one on a fruit tree in spring.

clue.text: They're shadows of their former selves

definitions.text: They're shadows of their former selves

parts.words: They're shadows of their former selves
parts.note: the idiom for people diminished by age or illness is taken literally: ghostly apparitions of the dead are shadowy forms of the people they once were

explanation.surface: People worn down until they are much weaker than they used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The everyday idiom about decline is read literally as ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: Wraiths are ghosts or spectral figures, literally shadowy versions of people who once lived.

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Examining a financial loss in investments.
explanation.walkthrough: CONSOLS are British government bonds with no fixed redemption date; 'Study loss' poses as reviewing a bad investment, while 'involved' scrambles the second word into SOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Consols are a type of British government stock, so they are securities.

parts.note: well-earned is read as earned from a well, money made by boring into the ground for oil or water

explanation.surface: Someone whose income is thoroughly deserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-earned' means deserved, but here it means earned from wells.
explanation.definitionFit: A driller bores wells for oil or water, so his pay literally comes from wells.

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following letters are taken out

parts.note: liquorice is a chewy black sweet

explanation.surface: A spirit served sweet and with no ice cubes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like a description of the drink, but it is the confectionery LIQUORICE; 'without' removes ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is alcoholic drink, especially distilled spirits.

parts.note: what is followed by something comes first, then the other, so this gives the word then

explanation.surface: A capital letter A with an S coming after it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital A' looks like an upper-case letter, but 'Capital' is the definition and the rest reads A THEN S.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.

clue.text: The standard aimed at by golfers

definitions.meaning: a standard is a banner or ...
on a golf green the hole is marked by a pin with a ..., which players aim their approach shots at

explanation.definitionFit: A flag is both a banner, or standard, and the marker on the pin golfers aim for on the green.

parts.note: read as putting an edge on, that is sharpening a blade, rather than making someone nervous

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on edge' suggests making someone anxious; read it as putting an edge on a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: To whet is to sharpen a knife or blade, giving it a keen edge.

clue.text: Describing one who was his own master?

definitions.text: Describing one who was his own master?

parts.words: Describing one who was his own master?
parts.note: master is read as teacher, so a person who was his own teacher learned without instruction from anyone else

explanation.surface: Words about someone who answered to nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his own master' usually means independent; here a master is a schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-taught learned without a teacher, acting as his own schoolmaster.

definitions.meaning: a slope or tilt
to speak with insincere, sanctimonious piety

explanation.definitionFit: Cant means both a slant or tilt and pious, hypocritical talk, so the verb fits the second sense.

clue.text: He tries to give the Three Wise Men free treats

parts.note: the Magi are the three wise men who visited the infant Jesus

indicators.note: set free, the letters of the word next to it are released into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to hand out free gifts to the Magi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He tries' sounds like effort, but it means a person who tries cases in court. 'free' turns TREATS into STRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a judicial officer who tries cases in a lower court.
